Date: 2027-05-01T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Weekly priorities & decisions — leadership readout (QBR inputs)

Team — attaching a concise pack ahead of Wednesday's QBR prep call. TL;DR of this week (wins / risks / asks):

Wins:
- Hosted API latency improvements: 95th p95 latency dropped 18% after the kernel selection change (INF-8423).
- Two new pilot customers live on Dedicated; combined commit ~120k/mo effective June.
- Optimize recommendations prototype yielded 12% token-cost reduction in staging.

Top risks / blockers:
1) SLA exception for Partner X (Acme) needs legal/procurement OK — procurement is asking for a firm incident-response window. See attached SLA_exception_request.pdf.
2) Model regression signal for summarization under long-context (seq > 8k) showing 6% ROUGE drop vs baseline — requires either rollback or targeted evals this week.
3) Capacity planning for EU region in June: Dedicated pool forecast is tight if demand follows pilot conversion.

Asks (actionable):
- Laura: escalate procurement timing with Acme and confirm contract signature ETA by Fri EOD.
- Markus/Marcus: triage long-context regression; propose rollback window or mitigation by Tue 5/4.
- Maya & Vivek: confirm EU capacity buffer and proposed burst plan; present cost delta for +20% reserve.

Attachments: QBR_input_v2.xlsx, Priorities_onepager.pdf, SLA_exception_request.pdf
Related: Drive folder (link in metadata), Jira INF-8423

I kept this intentionally short — happy to expand on any line in the QBR slot.

—Naomi

Date: 2027-05-01T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly priorities & decisions — leadership readout (QBR inputs)

Naomi — thanks for the crisp summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs before the QBR so we can agree on the decision path:

1) Regression: is the 6% ROUGE drop isolated to a single model build or observed across variants? If it's the latter, my bias is to roll back the last quantization patch for production and run the eval set against the previous build.

2) SLA exception: procurement@solsys.io is on cc for visibility (Proc team). If Acme requires a guaranteed 30-minute incident response, that's a partial SLA change. Legal will need the redline; Naomi, can you confirm whether Acme is asking for that as part of the initial contract or only for Dedicated pilots?

Action: Marcus, can you start the regression triage and post an initial RCA by EOD Mon (5/3)? If you need a hotfix window I can clear capacity from the rollout calendar.

—Markus

Thanks all — quick status update before tomorrow's prep slot:

- Marcus: triage underway; initial signal points to the new quant path on the 7.2 build. Marcus is proposing a scoped rollback to 7.1 for production traffic > 4k tokens; he'll post the RCA by 10:00 PT Mon (5/4).
- Procurement: Acme is OK with 1-hour during pilot; they want 30-minute for GA. Laura, please coordinate legal redline and we should confirm whether we will accept that for Dedicated customers vs. full GA.
- EU capacity: Maya & Vivek will present an option 1 ( +20% reserve ) and option 2 (on-demand burst with slightly higher unit cost) during QBR prep.

Next steps (owners):
- Marcus Lin: RCA + rollback plan (if needed) — due Mon 5/4 10:00 PT.
- Laura Bennett: legal/procurement timing & redline for Acme SLA — update Tue 5/5 EOD.
- Maya & Vivek: capacity options and cost delta — present Wed 5/6 QBR prep slot.

I'll update the Drive pack with Marcus' RCA and a short decision table. Thanks for the quick turn here.
